traditional_uses: The dried fruit is used in Ayurveda, including as one component of Triphala.
Traditional systems describe digestive and respiratory uses, but this does not establish clinical effectiveness.
preparation_notes: Do not infer a dose or preparation from image identification.
Use only authenticated, contaminant-tested products under qualified professional guidance.
Belleric Myrobalan.safety_warning: Evidence for interactions, pregnancy, and long-term medicinal use is limited. Avoid self-treatment with concentrated extracts.
Belleric Myrobalan.medical_disclaimer: Traditional-use information is educational and is not medical advice or proof of effectiveness.

traditional_uses: Widely used as a culinary spice.
Traditionally included in digestive preparations and mixtures intended to improve absorption.
preparation_notes: Normal culinary quantities are the lowest-risk form of use.
Do not use concentrated piperine products without checking medicine interactions.
Black Pepper.safety_warning: Concentrated piperine may change medicine absorption or metabolism and can irritate the digestive tract.
Black Pepper.medical_disclaimer: This information is educational and does not recommend medicinal dosing.

traditional_uses: The fruit is used in Ayurveda and is one component of Triphala.
Traditional practice includes digestive uses, although clinical evidence varies.
preparation_notes: Use authenticated preparations rather than unidentified gathered fruit.
Preparation and dose should be determined by a qualified professional.
Chebulic Myrobalan.safety_warning: May cause gastrointestinal effects and may be unsuitable with some medicines, during pregnancy, or before surgery.
Chebulic Myrobalan.medical_disclaimer: Traditional use is not evidence that a preparation is safe or effective for a disease.

traditional_uses: Used as a culinary spice and in traditional oral-care preparations.
Clove oil has a history of short-term topical dental use.
preparation_notes: Prefer food-level use; essential oil should never be swallowed or applied undiluted.
Dental pain requires professional assessment rather than repeated home treatment.
Clove.safety_warning: Clove oil can burn tissue and can be toxic if swallowed, especially for children. It may increase bleeding risk.
Clove.medical_disclaimer: This information does not replace dental or medical care.

traditional_uses: Used as food and traditionally for bowel regularity.
Ground seed is used as a dietary source of fibre and alpha-linolenic acid.
preparation_notes: Use food-grade seed with adequate fluid and follow labelled food guidance.
Avoid consuming raw or unripe seed in large amounts.
Flax Seed.safety_warning: May cause bloating or diarrhoea and affect medicine absorption. Seek advice during pregnancy or with anticoagulant or diabetes medicines.
Flax Seed.medical_disclaimer: This app does not prescribe treatment.

traditional_uses: Widely used as food and traditionally for cardiovascular and respiratory wellness.
Clinical research has studied supplements, but effects depend on the preparation.
preparation_notes: Food-level culinary use is preferable to homemade concentrated remedies.
Discuss supplements with a clinician and disclose them before surgery.
Garlic.safety_warning: Supplements can increase bleeding risk and interact with medicines. Raw topical garlic can cause serious skin burns.
Garlic.medical_disclaimer: This information is not treatment advice.

traditional_uses: The fruit is used as food and in Ayurvedic preparations.
Traditional use includes digestive and general-wellness preparations.
preparation_notes: Use correctly identified, food-grade ripe fruit or regulated products.
Do not extrapolate food use to concentrated medicinal doses.
Gooseberry.safety_warning: Concentrated products may affect blood glucose, bleeding, or medicines; pregnancy safety data are limited.
Gooseberry.medical_disclaimer: This is educational traditional-use information, not a recommendation to treat disease.

traditional_uses: Used in some traditional skin preparations.
Its psoralens have strong biological and light-sensitizing effects.
preparation_notes: Do not prepare or apply this fruit at home.
Psoralen-related treatment requires professional diagnosis, controlled dosing, and protection.
Psoralea Fruit.safety_warning: High risk: can cause severe photosensitivity, burns, eye injury, liver injury, and medicine interactions.
Psoralea Fruit.medical_disclaimer: Identification is not authorization for use; seek specialist guidance.

traditional_uses: Used as a culinary spice and in traditional digestive preparations.
It must be distinguished from toxic Japanese star anise and related species.
preparation_notes: Use only packaged food-grade spice from a traceable supplier.
Do not make medicinal tea for infants or use wild-collected fruits.
Star Anise.safety_warning: Toxic look-alike contamination can cause seizures. Image identification alone is insufficient for consumption.
Star Anise.medical_disclaimer: This app cannot certify that a specimen is safe to eat.

traditional_uses: Used as food, colouring, and in traditional digestive and skin preparations.
Curcumin research does not establish it as a replacement for medical treatment.
preparation_notes: Culinary use is different from high-dose extracts.
Use regulated products and consult a clinician before supplement use.
Turmeric.safety_warning: Concentrates may cause digestive effects, interact with medicines, worsen gallbladder problems, or contribute to liver injury.
Turmeric.medical_disclaimer: This app does not recommend a dose or treatment.

traditional_uses: Leaves are traditionally used in South Asian respiratory preparations.
Traditional use does not establish effectiveness for acute breathing problems.
preparation_notes: Do not calculate a preparation or dose from image identification.
Breathing difficulty requires urgent clinical assessment.
Adathoda.safety_warning: Avoid medicinal use during pregnancy and without professional review because active alkaloids and interactions are possible.
Adathoda.medical_disclaimer: This information is historical and educational, not respiratory treatment advice.

traditional_uses: Referenced in traditional external preparations in parts of South Asia.
The plant also has cultural and ornamental uses.
preparation_notes: Do not prepare this plant for home medicinal use.
Avoid the milky latex; wash exposed skin and eyes promptly with water.
Crown Flower.safety_warning: Poisonous: latex can injure skin and eyes, and ingestion can affect the heart and cause severe poisoning.
Crown Flower.medical_disclaimer: Seek urgent poison or medical advice after exposure; identification is not a use recommendation.

traditional_uses: Historically referenced in highly controlled traditional preparations.
Historical use does not make household use safe.
preparation_notes: Do not ingest, brew, smoke, or apply any part of Datura.
Keep seeds and plants inaccessible to children and animals.
Datura.safety_warning: Highly poisonous: can cause delirium, dangerous heart rate, overheating, seizures, coma, and death.
Datura.medical_disclaimer: No home preparation is provided. Suspected exposure is an emergency.

traditional_uses: Some Hibiscus species are used in beverages, foods, hair care, and traditional preparations.
Uses cannot be transferred safely between species by appearance.
preparation_notes: Verify the exact species before food or herbal use.
Use food-grade material rather than pesticide-treated ornamental flowers.
Hibiscus.safety_warning: May affect blood pressure or glucose and interact with medicines. Pregnancy use needs clinical advice.
Hibiscus.medical_disclaimer: The dataset label is not species-specific and does not certify edibility.

traditional_uses: Certain Lonicera flower buds are used in East Asian traditional preparations.
Different species have different safety profiles.
preparation_notes: Do not prepare from a common-name image identification.
Require botanical verification and a regulated source.
Honey Suckle.safety_warning: Some berries and plant parts can be toxic; safety cannot be generalized across species.
Honey Suckle.medical_disclaimer: Exact species verification is required before any use.

traditional_uses: Food-grade petals and rose water are used in foods, fragrances, and traditional skin preparations.
Ornamental roses are not automatically food-grade.
preparation_notes: Use only pesticide-free, food-grade material.
Do not ingest essential oil or apply concentrates to damaged skin.
Rose.safety_warning: Possible allergy or irritation; ornamental flowers may contain pesticide residues.
Rose.medical_disclaimer: This common-name identification does not certify edibility.

traditional_uses: No medicinal use is provided because this name refers to many unrelated species.
Visual similarity is insufficient for safe botanical identification.
preparation_notes: Do not ingest or prepare this flower from the dataset label.
Obtain a botanical species identification first.
Yellow Daisy.safety_warning: Unknown species may cause allergy, dermatitis, toxicity, or interactions.
Yellow Daisy.medical_disclaimer: Verify and relabel the scientific species before adding medicinal information.

traditional_uses: Flowers are used as food colouring and a beverage ingredient in parts of Asia.
The plant is referenced in traditional cognitive and general-wellness preparations.
preparation_notes: Use correctly identified, pesticide-free, food-grade flowers.
Traditional medicinal dosing requires qualified guidance.
shankupushpam.safety_warning: May cause digestive effects or allergy; pregnancy and medicine-interaction evidence is limited.
shankupushpam.medical_disclaimer: Food tradition and preliminary research do not prove treatment effectiveness.

traditional_uses: Widely consumed as food and used in traditional respiratory and skin preparations.
preparation_notes: Prefer normal culinary use; do not apply raw onion to damaged skin.
Allium cepa (Onion).safety_warning: Can irritate skin and digestion, cause allergy, and may affect bleeding or blood glucose in concentrated forms.
Allium cepa (Onion).medical_disclaimer: Food use does not establish a medicinal treatment.

traditional_uses: Ripe fruit and cooked unripe fruit are foods; several plant parts appear in regional traditional practice.
preparation_notes: Use edible fruit as food and do not prepare leaves, latex, bark, or extracts without expert verification.
Artocarpus heterophyllus (Jackfruit).safety_warning: Possible latex or birch-pollen cross-allergy; concentrated preparations may affect blood glucose.
Artocarpus heterophyllus (Jackfruit).medical_disclaimer: This record does not recommend non-food plant parts.

traditional_uses: Traditionally used in Ayurveda for memory and cognitive wellness.
preparation_notes: Use authenticated products because several different plants share the name Brahmi; dosing needs professional review.
Bacopa monnieri (Bhrami).safety_warning: May cause digestive effects and interact with thyroid, sedative, or other medicines; pregnancy safety is uncertain.
Bacopa monnieri (Bhrami).medical_disclaimer: Traditional cognitive use is not proof of treatment effectiveness.

traditional_uses: Bamboo shoots and other parts have food, material, and regional traditional uses.
preparation_notes: Do not eat raw shoots; edible shoots require species verification and proper processing to reduce cyanogenic compounds.
Bambusa vulgaris (Bamboo).safety_warning: Raw or incorrectly processed shoots may release cyanide. Leaves and ornamental material are not certified food ingredients.
Bambusa vulgaris (Bamboo).medical_disclaimer: Image identification cannot establish safe edibility or processing.

traditional_uses: Commonly cooked as a leafy vegetable and used in food-based traditional preparations.
preparation_notes: Wash and cook food-grade leaves; avoid material collected from polluted or pesticide-treated sites.
Basella alba (Malabar Spinach).safety_warning: Frequent medicinal use may be unsuitable for people on restricted oxalate diets or with kidney-stone risk.
Basella alba (Malabar Spinach).medical_disclaimer: This is food and identification information, not dietary treatment advice.

traditional_uses: Leaves and seeds are used as foods; mustard oil and poultices appear in traditional practice.
preparation_notes: Use regulated food products; do not apply strong homemade mustard poultices because they can burn skin.
Brassica Juncea (Indian Mustard).safety_warning: Can cause allergy and skin burns; concentrated or unregulated oil is not appropriate for infants or medicinal ingestion.
Brassica Juncea (Indian Mustard).medical_disclaimer: Culinary use does not validate topical or medicinal remedies.

traditional_uses: Consumed as a vegetable; leaves and swollen stems are used in food preparations.
preparation_notes: Wash and prepare as food rather than as a concentrated remedy.
Brassica oleracea (Kohlrabi).safety_warning: Large dietary changes may matter for thyroid disease or anticoagulant therapy; obtain individualized advice.
Brassica oleracea (Kohlrabi).medical_disclaimer: Nutritional information is not medical treatment guidance.

traditional_uses: Historically referenced in controlled external preparations and cultural practices.
preparation_notes: Do not prepare at home and avoid contact with milky latex.
Calotropis gigantea (Crown flower_Ekka).safety_warning: Poisonous: latex damages eyes and skin; ingestion can cause dangerous cardiac poisoning.
Calotropis gigantea (Crown flower_Ekka).medical_disclaimer: Suspected exposure requires urgent medical or poison advice.

traditional_uses: Used as food; capsaicin preparations have traditional and regulated topical pain uses.
preparation_notes: Use culinary amounts or regulated topical products; wash hands and avoid eyes, broken skin, and inhalation.
Capsicum annuum (Chilly).safety_warning: Can cause severe burning, breathing irritation, or gastrointestinal symptoms. Keep concentrated products from children.
Capsicum annuum (Chilly).medical_disclaimer: Do not make concentrated topical remedies from identified leaves or fruit.

traditional_uses: Used in some South Asian traditional external and joint-comfort preparations.
preparation_notes: Require botanical confirmation and qualified guidance; do not apply homemade preparations to inflamed or broken skin.
Cardiospermum halicacabum (Balloon Vine).safety_warning: Reliable dosing, interaction, pregnancy, and long-term safety information is limited.
Cardiospermum halicacabum (Balloon Vine).medical_disclaimer: Traditional use is not evidence of safety or clinical effectiveness.

traditional_uses: Ripe fruit is eaten as food; latex, leaves, and unripe fruit have varied traditional uses.
preparation_notes: Prefer ripe fruit as food; do not make leaf juice or latex remedies without clinical supervision.
Carica papaya (Papaya).safety_warning: Latex can cause allergy and tissue irritation; unripe fruit and medicinal preparations may be unsafe in pregnancy and can interact with medicines.
Carica papaya (Papaya).medical_disclaimer: The app does not recommend papaya leaf preparations for treating illness.

traditional_uses: Ripe fruit is used in foods, preserves, and regional traditional preparations.
preparation_notes: Use correctly identified ripe, food-grade fruit; avoid milky latex and non-food plant parts.
Carissa Carandas (Karanda).safety_warning: Unripe material and latex may irritate; evidence for concentrated medicinal products and interactions is limited.
Carissa Carandas (Karanda).medical_disclaimer: Food tradition does not establish medicinal dosing.

traditional_uses: Historically used in folk medicine and is the source plant for important prescription anticancer compounds.
preparation_notes: Do not ingest or prepare any part as a home remedy; pharmaceutical compounds require controlled manufacturing and oncology supervision.
Catharanthus roseus (Catharanthus).safety_warning: Potentially poisonous and can affect blood cells, nerves, pregnancy, and many medicines. Keep away from children and animals.
Catharanthus roseus (Catharanthus).medical_disclaimer: A medicinal source plant is not a safe homemade cancer treatment.

traditional_uses: Leaves are promoted in some traditional practices for blood-glucose support.
preparation_notes: Do not replace diabetes medicine or monitoring with leaf preparations; discuss use with a diabetes clinician.
Chamaecostus cuspidatus (Insulin).safety_warning: May contribute to low blood glucose or interact with diabetes treatment; product quality and dosing are not standardized.
Chamaecostus cuspidatus (Insulin).medical_disclaimer: This plant is not insulin and does not replace evidence-based diabetes care.

traditional_uses: Camphor has historical aromatic and external uses in regulated products.
preparation_notes: Do not distil, ingest, or make concentrated preparations from leaves; use only regulated products exactly as labelled.
Cinnamomum camphora (Camphor).safety_warning: Camphor is poisonous if swallowed and can cause seizures; concentrated vapour or skin exposure is especially unsafe for children.
Cinnamomum camphora (Camphor).medical_disclaimer: Suspected ingestion requires urgent poison-control or emergency advice.

traditional_uses: Fruit and juice are foods and are used in traditional beverages and household preparations.
preparation_notes: Use food-grade fruit; dilute acidic juice and do not apply essential oil or juice to damaged skin.
Citrus limon (Lemon).safety_warning: Acid can damage teeth or irritate skin, and peel oil may increase sunlight sensitivity or allergy.
Citrus limon (Lemon).medical_disclaimer: Lemon preparations do not replace treatment for infection or other disease.

traditional_uses: Fruit and peel are used in foods, preserves, fragrance, and regional digestive preparations.
preparation_notes: Use food-grade fruit and avoid concentrated peel oil on skin.
Citrus medica (herelikai).safety_warning: Citrus acids and oils may irritate, affect teeth, trigger allergy, or increase sunlight sensitivity.
Citrus medica (herelikai).medical_disclaimer: Traditional digestive use is not a disease-treatment recommendation.

traditional_uses: Roasted seeds are consumed as a caffeinated beverage; leaves are used in some regional drinks.
preparation_notes: Use regulated food products and account for total daily caffeine; do not prepare unidentified raw plant parts medicinally.
Coffea arabica (Coffee).safety_warning: Caffeine can worsen anxiety, sleep, palpitations, reflux, or blood pressure and requires caution in pregnancy and with medicines.
Coffea arabica (Coffee).medical_disclaimer: This app does not recommend caffeine for treating fatigue or disease.

traditional_uses: Aromatic leaves are used as seasoning and in regional respiratory and digestive preparations.
preparation_notes: Use correctly identified, food-grade leaves in modest culinary quantities; medicinal preparations need qualified guidance.
Coleus amboinicus (Mexican mint_Doddpath.safety_warning: Concentrated extracts and essential oils may irritate or interact with medicines; pregnancy and child safety data are limited.
Coleus amboinicus (Mexican mint_Doddpath.medical_disclaimer: Traditional use does not replace assessment for breathing or digestive symptoms.
